title: Normalized realization of scalar comparisons on quotient systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings and chosen uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $f:X\to Y$ with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $D=E,L$ and $W=X,Y$ put $A^D_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_D/\varpi_D^n)_W$ and $R_{D,W}=\lim_nA^D_{W,n}$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the coefficient homomorphisms $i_n:A^E_{W,n}\to A^L_{W,n}$ induced by the valuation-ring inclusion, the actual quotient transitions, and completed scalar extension $\widehat S_W$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Write $\mathcal R_D\dashv\mathcal L_D$ for coherent reduction and total derived limit of restricted strict systems, with counit $e_D$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A system is normalized when each derived transition-adjoint is an isomorphism [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Let $F_D,T_D$ denote finite-system derived pullback and tensor, $S_W$ finite-system derived scalar extension, and $\widehat F_D,\widehat T_D$ the completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]; the finite-system operations are those on the ordinary derived categories of strict semilinear systems [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

For flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$ of $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], all complexes obtained from $P_n=P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}A^E_{Y,n}$ and $Q_n$ by scalar extension, finite pullback and signed total tensor are flat-term K-flat. The simultaneous isomorphisms
$$(P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}A^E_{Y,n})\otimes_{A^E_{Y,n}}A^L_{Y,n}\cong P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}A^L_{Y,n},\quad(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes i_n(a)b$$
(and their insertion-of-one inverses) identify the scalar quotient systems, with every transition, with the normalized systems computing $\widehat S_YM,\widehat S_YN$ [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model]. Their finite pullback and tensor systems, including those for the integral pullback and tensor inputs, are normalized as well.

There exist representative-normalized realizations
$$\widehat F_D\cong\mathcal L_DF_D\mathcal R_D,\quad
\widehat T_D\cong\mathcal L_DT_D(\mathcal R_D,\mathcal R_D),\quad
\widehat S_W\cong\mathcal L_LS_W\mathcal R_E.$$
Normalization means that on every simultaneous flat-term K-flat quotient presentation these isomorphisms are induced by the actual quotient maps, the displayed balanced association, the signed total tensor generators, and the coherent counit, with the K-injective-normalized total-limit/Roos comparison of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. In particular their existence and the assertions below concern the specified completed operations and their maps, not just isomorphic objects.

Let $r_F:\mathcal R_D\widehat F_D\to F_D\mathcal R_D$, $r_T:\mathcal R_D\widehat T_D\to T_D(\mathcal R_D,\mathcal R_D)$ and $r_S:\mathcal R_L\widehat S\to S\mathcal R_E$ be reduction of these realizations followed by $e_D$ or $e_L$. They are isomorphisms on the displayed normalized inputs. The ordinary tensor scalar comparison has a unique derived-system localization $\sigma^D: S T_E\cong T_L(S,S)$ characterized on all flat-term K-flat representatives by inserting the universal scalar-change counits and the fixed K-flat tensor model isomorphisms; similarly $\kappa^D:S_XF_E\cong F_LS_Y$ is the localization of balanced scalar association [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. For the pullback and tensor scalar comparisons $a_F,a_T$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] with their canonical tensor-association normalization, the following equations hold in the derived category of entire coefficient systems:
$$F_L(r_{S,Y})\,r_{F,L}\,\mathcal R_L(a_F)
=\kappa^D_{\mathcal R_EM}\,S_X(r_{F,E})\,r_{S,X},$$
$$T_L(r_S,r_S)\,r_{T,L}\,\mathcal R_L(a_T)
=\sigma^D_{\mathcal R_EM,\mathcal R_EN}\,S(r_{T,E})\,r_S.$$
All evaluations and quotient transitions are retained in these equations. Consequently, under the normalized source and target realizations, $a_F$ and $a_T$ are respectively $\mathcal L_L(\kappa^D)$ and $\mathcal L_L(\sigma^D)$, naturally in the inputs and independently of resolutions through their canonical comparisons. No flatness of $A^E_{W,n}\to A^L_{W,n}$, or interchange of an operation with arbitrary inverse limits, is asserted.

source.place: Agent extraction of old scalar-extension-tower-coherence proof steps 1--2 and 8--9; Stacks Tag 06YS, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-K-flat-resolution, and Tag 0G7E, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-pullback-K-flat, for the representative calculus; the normalized completion comparison is the agent argument refining the blueprint integral-operations clause.

proof.text: Work with the strict semilinear system categories of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], on fixed small presentations of the pro-etale topoi. Its scalar and tensor functors are constructed on the derived category of the ringed sequence topos, and its geometric inverse image is the whole-system inverse image. The constant-coefficient structure maps are the isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Naturality of the constant-sheaf construction makes their squares with $i_n$ and every quotient map commute. Thus these are precisely the finite $S_W,F_D,T_D$ in the statement, with their actual transitions. We will construct maps on this category, retaining its coherent counit from [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

source.place: Finite operations clause; passage to the ringed sequence site is the agent refinement.

proof.text: The input resolutions exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] successively to $R_{E,Y}\to A^E_{Y,n}\to A^L_{Y,n}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] to each finite ringed-topos pullback. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] whenever a signed direct-sum total tensor is taken. Each conclusion gives both K-flatness and flatness of every term; its output therefore satisfies the hypotheses for the next operation. This induction proves the asserted closure for all the displayed models, including iterated operations and unbounded resolutions. No map of coefficient rings is required to be flat.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat); their stated general ringed-site versions.

proof.text: The association map in the statement and its inverse are balanced: $((x a)\otimes a')\otimes b$ and $(x\otimes aa')\otimes b$ have the same image, and the second balancing relation is exactly multiplication by $i_n(a')$. The inverse inserts $1$ in the $A^E_n$ factor. For $m\ge n$ the two routes on $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ give $x\otimes q^L_{m,n}(i_m(a)b)=x\otimes i_n(q^E_{m,n}a)q^L_{m,n}b$. Consequently these are inverse chain maps of entire strict systems. By [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] the resulting system $(P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}A^L_{Y,n})_n$ is normalized and its coherent reduction comparison with $\widehat S_YM$ is the specified counit followed by inverse association. Apply the same statement to $Q$ and to every ambient integral input that occurs below; it has no boundedness or constructibility hypothesis.

source.place: Integral/common-stage clause; simultaneous balanced quotient association and its transition square.

proof.text: The reduction $\mathcal R_DK$ is normalized for every ambient $K$, and the actual reconstruction counit is invertible on normalized systems, by [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps]. Finite pullback and tensor preserve normalization: for a normalized $A$ the pullback transition-adjoint identifies with $F_n(\alpha^A_{m,n})$ under quotient/pullback association; for normalized $A,B$ the tensor transition-adjoint identifies with $T_n(\alpha^A_{m,n},\alpha^B_{m,n})$ under quotient/tensor association. These associations are the monoidal composition comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], applied also to scalar extension along the quotient. Their naturality identifies the actual transition, by transposing its scalar-adjunction unit. Both displayed maps are invertible. Scalar extension also preserves normalization: the quotient-association comparison identifies its transition-adjoint with $S_n(\alpha^A_{m,n})$. Thus all intermediate finite systems used in the two equations are normalized, including the reductions of the integral operation inputs.

source.place: Integral operations clause; normalization by the transition adjoints, using the sequence-category operations.

proof.text: Let $\rho_F,\rho_T$ denote the natural functor identifications supplied by [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]. These realize the specified $\widehat F_D,\widehat T_D$ as $\mathcal L_DF_D\mathcal R_D$ and $\mathcal L_DT_D(\mathcal R_D,\mathcal R_D)$ with their actual quotient representatives. For scalar extension, association from Step 3 identifies the defining restricted Roos tower of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] with $U_LS\mathcal R_E$. Apply the natural comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] to obtain $\rho_S:\widehat S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_LS\mathcal R_E$. Exactness of countable products needed here holds by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. That comparison is normalized on K-injective tower resolutions by the ordinary limit cone, with zero shifted coordinate, and respects strict augmentations. Thus all three realizations have precisely the representative and total-limit normalization required in the statement.

source.place: Integral clause: the defining quotient/Roos models and their total-derived-limit comparison.

proof.text: Define $r_H=e_{H\mathcal R(-)}\mathcal R(\rho_H)$ for $H=F,T,S$, with the indicated coefficient on each reduction. For $T$ there are two input reductions. These are whole-system maps by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Steps 3--4 put the systems on their right in the normalized subcategory. Hence $e$ is invertible by [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps], and $\rho_H$ is invertible by Step 5; all the $r_H$ are isomorphisms. On scalar-extension inputs this is exactly the coherent counit comparison of [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model], by its stated formula and the association used to define $\rho_S$.

source.place: Normalized coherent reduction of the actual completed-operation realizations.

proof.text: On the ringed sequence topos the simultaneous chain maps $\kappa,\sigma$ are those of [lem-pur-strict-coefficient-comparison-calculus], for $R^0=A^E$, $R^1=A^L$ (take $R^2=R^1$ if a three-stage package is desired). Its formulas and inverse formulas are maps of strict systems, with both differential summands and every transition. Use the actual normalized scalar adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] and the canonical derived tensor representative model of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-tensor-comparison] on this sequence site: its full representative square is exactly the localization of $\sigma$ with the universal scalar counits and K-flat tensor model comparisons, as packaged in [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data]. For $\kappa$, the ordinary scalar-association maps descend by the composition and geometric-isomorphism comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. All these are isomorphisms on derived system categories. Uniqueness of the tensor localization is [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] on the same ringed site; the pullback localization is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] on the resolving presentation. This constructs the specified $\sigma^D,\kappa^D$, rather than trying to lift arbitrary evaluated arrows.

source.place: Finite pullback/tensor clause, scalar-association localization; Tags 07A4 and 0D6D supply the underlying ringed-pullback calculus.

proof.text:
For the pullback equation set $A_F=S_XF_E\mathcal R_EM$ and $B_F=F_LS_Y\mathcal R_EM$, and define
$$\beta_{A_F}=\mathcal L_LS_X(r_{F,E})\,\rho_{S,X},\qquad
\beta_{B_F}=\mathcal L_LF_L(r_{S,Y})\,\rho_{F,L}.$$
Their domains are respectively $\widehat S_X\widehat F_EM$ and $\widehat F_L\widehat S_YM$. For tensor set $A_T=ST_E(\mathcal R_EM,\mathcal R_EN)$, $B_T=T_L(S\mathcal R_EM,S\mathcal R_EN)$, with
$$\beta_{A_T}=\mathcal L_LS(r_{T,E})\,\rho_S,\qquad
\beta_{B_T}=\mathcal L_LT_L(r_S,r_S)\,\rho_{T,L}.$$
All are isomorphisms. Write $c_H,d_H$ for the right-side and left-side reduction-coordinate composites before $\mathcal R_L(a_H)$ in the question. Naturality of the whole-system counit of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] gives
$$c_H=e_{A_H}\mathcal R_L(\beta_{A_H}),\qquad d_H=e_{B_H}\mathcal R_L(\beta_{B_H})\quad(H=F,T).$$
For example $e_{S_XF_E\mathcal R_EM}\mathcal R_L\mathcal L_LS_X(r_{F,E})=S_X(r_{F,E})e_{S_X\mathcal R_E\widehat F_EM}$. This proves the coordinate identity in the system category.

source.place: Agent coordinate calculation: recursively insert the same coherent counit into the source and target words.

proof.text: We will use the actual reduction-adjunction unit, including its augmentation normalization. In [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction], the Hom bijection is the derived fraction extension of the ordinary tensor/limit correspondence. For a flat-term K-flat $V$, resolve its strict quotient system by $q:\mathcal R V\to I$ on the sequence site. The identity of $\mathcal RV$ is represented by $q$. The ordinary adjunction sends $q$ to the chain map $V\to\lim I$ given by $v\mapsto(q_n(v\otimes1))_n$; this is the derived unit under that Hom bijection. The right-derived-limit identification of [lem-coef-sequence-pushforward-limit-projections] transports this same adjunction to $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$. By the strict-augmentation normalization in [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], the quotient product map with zero shifted coordinate gives the same map after the resolution and the ordinary-limit inclusion. Thus $u_V$ is precisely the strict quotient augmentation in the specified total-limit/Roos coordinates. This comparison uses the ordinary derived-adjunction correspondence on a resolution, not faithfulness of evaluations.

source.place: Derived ringed-site adjunction applied to the sequence projection, and the strict augmentation normalization of total derived limit; agent calculation using the cited derived Hom correspondence.

proof.text:
Put $\alpha_F=\kappa^D_{\mathcal R_EM}$, $\alpha_T=\sigma^D_{\mathcal R_EM,\mathcal R_EN}$ and construct
$$a_H^0=\beta_{B_H}^{-1}\mathcal L_L(\alpha_H)\beta_{A_H}\quad(H=F,T).$$
These are natural isomorphisms of the actual completed-operation words. We now verify their canonical tensor-association normalization; this is needed to identify their arrows with $a_F,a_T$, not merely their objects. Use [lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models] to write the underlying integral pullback or tensor as $C_EU$, where $C_D=\mathcal L_D\mathcal R_D$, $U=F^{\rm amb}_EM$ or $U=M\otimes^L_{R_E}N$. Its identification respects the actual quotient augmentation $u_U:U\to C_EU$. Write $B_W=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ for ambient scalar change. On complete inputs the actual comparison $\chi:B_WK\to\widehat S_WK$ is the quotient-augmentation isomorphism of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Consequently the augmentation into the source word is
$$\nu_H:B_WU\xrightarrow{B_W(u_U)}B_WC_EU\xrightarrow{\chi_{C_EU}}\widehat S_WC_EU.$$
Here $W=X$ for pullback and $W=Y$ for tensor; $C_EU$ is complete by Step 4 and reconstruction.

source.place: Agent verification of the canonical completed comparison, using the ambient operation models and their quotient augmentations.

proof.text: The source coordinate $\beta_{A_H}$ identifies $\nu_H$ with the canonical completion unit of $B_WU$. To check the map, use one flat-term K-flat representative $V$ of $U$. The entire reduction system of $B_WU$ is represented by $((V\otimes_{R_E}R_L)\otimes_{R_L}A^L_n)_n$, identified with $(V\otimes_{R_E}A^L_n)_n$ by multiplying the coefficient factors. Likewise $S\mathcal R_EU$ is represented by $((V\otimes_{R_E}A^E_n)\otimes_{A^E_n}A^L_n)_n$, with the same association. Both strict augmentations take $v\otimes b$ to $(v\otimes\bar b)_n$ and have zero shifted Roos coordinate. The normalization of $\chi$ in [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] uses exactly this strict augmentation. The inserted $u_U$ cancels the counit in $r_H$ by $e_{\mathcal R_EU}\mathcal R_E(u_U)=1$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; the ambient model comparison preserves that augmentation. Thus the assertion is an identity of strict augmentations followed by total-limit functoriality, using [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], not a deduction from equal evaluated maps.

source.place: Agent source normalization: strict quotient augmentation and the reduction-adjunction triangle identity.

proof.text:
For the target word use $\chi_M,\chi_N$ to replace $\widehat S$ of the complete inputs by ambient $B$; then [lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models] identifies that target with $C_LV_H$, where $V_F=F_L^{\rm amb}B_YM$ and $V_T=B_YM\otimes^L_{R_{L,Y}}B_YN$. The ambient coefficient comparisons
$$b_F:B_XF_E^{\rm amb}M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_L^{\rm amb}B_YM,\qquad
b_T:B_Y(M\otimes^L_{R_{E,Y}}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_YM\otimes^L_{R_{L,Y}}B_YN$$
are the canonical composition and tensor maps of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Reducing $b_H$ on simultaneous K-flat models gives precisely $\alpha_H$, under the associations in Step 11: for pullback both routes multiply the coefficient factors and insert $1$; for tensor both send $(x\otimes y)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes b)\otimes(y\otimes1)$. Differentiating gives the same two summands with $(-1)^{\deg x}$, and quotienting the coefficients before or after these formulas gives the same result. These are the strict maps of [lem-pur-strict-coefficient-comparison-calculus]. Naturality of the Roos comparison and the representative normalization of $\chi$ therefore show
$$a_H^0\nu_H=u_{V_H}b_H$$
in these target coordinates, as an equality obtained from the strict augmented towers.

source.place: Agent target normalization: scalar association on the strict augmented quotient models.

proof.text: The canonical tensor-association normalization of the integral scalar comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] means extending the ambient $b_H$ to the completed words with the quotient units: in the coordinates above it is the equation $a_H\nu_H=u_{V_H}b_H$. It specifies a unique arrow. Indeed [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus] gives an adjoint equivalence between complete objects and normalized systems; [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps] says that $\mathcal R_LZ$ is normalized for every ambient $Z$. The adjunction consequently makes $u_Z:Z\to C_LZ$ a reflection into complete objects: for complete $J$, precomposition gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C_LZ,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Z,J)$. This also follows directly by applying $\mathcal R_L\dashv\mathcal L_L$ and the inverse of $u_J$. Step 11 identifies $\nu_H$ with this unit, and the target $C_LV_H$ is complete. Step 12 proves that $a_H^0$ has the required normalization. Thus it is precisely the representative-normalized choice $a_H$ in the statement. This argument supplies and fixes that normalization of the existence isomorphisms; no normalization is inferred from the mere existence assertion of the cited scalar-extension theorem.

source.place: Agent normalization uniqueness: completion as reflection; this fixes the first two integral scalar comparison arrows.

proof.text:
For $H=F,T$, substitute $a_H=\beta_{B_H}^{-1}\mathcal L_L(\alpha_H)\beta_{A_H}$ into Step 8. Naturality of the actual counit [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] gives
$$d_H\mathcal R_L(a_H)=e_{B_H}\mathcal R_L\mathcal L_L(\alpha_H)\mathcal R_L(\beta_{A_H})=\alpha_H e_{A_H}\mathcal R_L(\beta_{A_H})=\alpha_Hc_H.$$
Expanding $c_F,d_F,c_T,d_T$ yields exactly the two equations in the question. All terms are morphisms in the derived category of whole systems, so all evaluations and transitions follow by functoriality. Applying $\mathcal L_L$ and the same inverse source and target coordinates gives the asserted integral-limit descriptions.

source.place: Agent counit naturality calculation yielding both displayed system equations.

proof.text: Every comparison used above is natural on the simultaneous K-flat models and preserves their quasi-isomorphism comparisons. Scalar and tensor localization and uniqueness from [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore give naturality for all input morphisms and independence from resolutions through their canonical comparisons. The total-limit comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] is itself natural and independent of its K-injective tower resolution. Thus the same statements hold for the actual completed maps. In Steps 3, 7, 10 and 11, quotient scalar changes were computed on K-flat inputs; their ring maps were never assumed flat. Limits were applied to already constructed strict system maps, and no operation was commuted with an arbitrary inverse limit.
